alignments.note: Construct noun אֹרֶךְ takes only its own English word; the chain's single written *the* belongs to the article morpheme on the rectum (rule 29).

The rectum's article takes the one *the* the ASV writes for this chain, fronted by English to the phrase's left edge while the rectum is rendered *each curtain* without an article of its own (rule 29's fronting clause); of the phrase's two articles the first takes it (rule 47). Competing reading: mark it `unrepresented` and treat *The* as a supplied article on the construct; rejected because rule 29 supplies a *the* only where no article morpheme is present and marks an article `unrepresented` only where the ASV writes no *the* for the phrase at all.

review_notes: Corrected on the same point as v. 9: in both measurement chains the single written *the* goes to the present article morpheme on the rectum, fronted onto the construct, rather than to a supplied article beside an `unrepresented` present article (rule 29, with rule 47 choosing the first of the two articles).
The predicate copula *was* joins the first numeral phrase under rule 20; the gapped second clause writes none.
*the eleven curtains* is a different case: no article morpheme stands there, so the supplied *the* belongs to the noun (rules 15, 46).
